news.headline: Deferred 100% US tariffs offer only temporary relief to India as Russian oil imports fall
news.story_lead: Deferred 100% US tariffs offer only temporary relief to India as Russian oil imports fall Refiners began reducing their exposure while the bill was still moving through Congress, before Trump signed the Russia and Iran Sanctions act into a law. Washington’s decision to hold off tariffs of up to 100% that a new US sanctions law would have triggered against India for buying Russian oil offers only temporary relief, people familiar with the matter said, as Indian refiners have already cut their Russian purchases and are paying more for the oil that replaced them. Imports of discounted Russian crude have fallen by a third since July, industry executives said, and India’s crude import bill rose 31.6% in September from August even though volumes grew only 14.2%, according to the petroleum ministry’s Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC).
news.full_article_text: Deferred 100% US tariffs offer only temporary relief to India as Russian oil imports fall Refiners began reducing their exposure while the bill was still moving through Congress, before Trump signed the Russia and Iran Sanctions act into a law. Washington’s decision to hold off tariffs of up to 100% that a new US sanctions law would have triggered against India for buying Russian oil offers only temporary relief, people familiar with the matter said, as Indian refiners have already cut their Russian purchases and are paying more for the oil that replaced them. Imports of discounted Russian crude have fallen by a third since July, industry executives said, and India’s crude import bill rose 31.6% in September from August even though volumes grew only 14.2%, according to the petroleum ministry’s Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC). Refiners began reducing their exposure while the bill was still moving through Congress , before US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (Graham Act) into law on September 18, company executives and industry experts said on condition of anonymity. They expected geopolitical conditions and the approaching US midterm elections to make it difficult for Washington to enforce the act from October 18, but stepped up imports from the US and other suppliers anyway. Also Read | Indian refiners de-risked in advance, Trump's Russia sanctions waiver a ‘temporary’ relief: Experts Imports of Russian crude have dropped to about 1.8 million barrels a day from around 2.7 million at the July peak, they said. Russian oil made up a negligible share of India’s crude imports until 2021-22. Its share rose to nearly a third in 2025-26, as Moscow, hit by Western sanctions, offered steep discounts. Refiners have replaced it with crude from the US, West Africa, South America and traditional West Asian suppliers, which costs more, partly because of higher freight and insurance charges, they said. Rising Costs and Import Bill In absolute terms, the import bill rose 31.6% in just one month to $15.4 billion in September from $11.7 billion in August, while volumes rose to 21.7 million tonnes from 19 million tonnes (a 14.21% increase), PPAC data show. In this period, average crude oil price of Indian basket increased by 28.71% from $90.19 a barrel in August 2026 to $116.09 per barrel in September 2026. Over April-September 2026-27, the crude import bill rose 46.4% to $90.6 billion, a period that also captured the surge in global oil prices after shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted. Also Read | Republican lawmaker hits out at Trump over Russia sanctions waiver, says he is 'prolonging the war, not ending it' Temporary Relief and Trade Leverage Experts attributed the higher bill to volatile global oil prices, driven by worsening geopolitical tensions, and to the threat the Graham Act posed to major energy importers such as India and China . That threat remains because the act’s secondary sanctions have only been deferred, they said, leaving Trump free to use the law against these countries whenever he chooses. The experts said the waiver offers no long-term assurance either for India’s energy security or for its trade talks with the US, in which New Delhi is seeking a comparative tariff advantage for Indian goods over competing countries. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that the first tranche of the trade agreement would be put into operation once India secured a “competitive advantage” over its peers. Ajay Srivastava, founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), a New Delhi-based trade think tank, said the US Trade Representative’s continued monitoring of Russian energy purchases would allow “Washington to review the waiver and retain the tariff threat as leverage in future negotiations”. “Under its October 9 agreement with Russia, the US decided to buy Russian diesel to ease domestic shortages and high fuel prices. Punishing other countries for buying Russian energy while doing so itself would invite accusations of double standards. Washington had also agreed not to raise tariffs on China until January 10 under a deal reached during President Xi Jinping’s US visit last month. With US spared, and China shielded, targeting India alone could derail ongoing bilateral trade negotiations,” he said. Also Read | 'Reward for Putin': Zelensky fears US sanctions relief to Russia, diesel deal not the end of it The message was clear, Srivastava said: US interests determined when penalties applied. “For India, the waiver buys time but offers no lasting certainty. Russia’s share of Indian oil imports fell from 51% in July to 44% in August as India bought more from the US, despite higher prices, and from the UAE. Yet SRIA [the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act] remains law, leaving Washington free to revive the tariff threat to extract concessions in bilateral trade talks,” he said. “India should protect its energy security, buy oil on commercial terms and prepare for renewed US pressure. Temporary tariff relief is no basis for permanent trade concessions,” he added. news.headline: Judicial-Led SIT to Probe Kolkata Pandal Stampede; State and Central Relief Packages Announced
news.story_lead: At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Maha Saptami evening. The West Bengal government has announced a Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe headed by a sitting Calcutta High Court judge. Financial compensation and support measures have been announced by both the state and central governments.
news.full_article_text:
### Overview of the Incident
On the evening of Saturday, October 17, 2026 (Maha Saptami), a tragic stampede occurred at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata. The incident resulted in the loss of at least 19 lives and left 25 people injured. Severe overcrowding, unexpected heavy rain, and a sudden rush following an announcement made by the organisers triggered the incident as people waiting outside surged forward.

### Judicial Probe & Investigative Action
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court will investigate the tragedy. The state government will formally request the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to nominate the sitting judge. The SIT will comprise personnel from the Special Task Force (STF), the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), and other state departments.

The Anti-Rowdy Section of the Kolkata Police has secured CCTV footage to reconstruct the exact sequence of events. Authorities have detained several puja committee members, private security personnel, and duty staff for questioning to determine responsibility for crowd-management failures.

### Compensation and Relief Measures
- **State Government Assistance:** The West Bengal government announced ₹25 lakh compensation and a Group D government job for the family of each deceased individual. Injured victims will receive ₹5 lakh each, with full medical expenses covered at any hospital of their choice.
- **Central Relief Assistance:** Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced ex-gratia relief from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) consisting of ₹2 lakh for the next of kin of each deceased person and ₹50,000 for each injured person.
- **Emergency Helplines:** The state government activated a toll-free helpline (1800-345-5678) and Kolkata Police established a dedicated control room helpline (033-2214-1310) for assistance.

### Crowd Control & Safety Directives
To mitigate further safety risks, authorities advised popular theme-based pandals across Kolkata to temporarily suspend visits. Kolkata hosts approximately 3,500 Durga Puja pandals annually, requiring extensive crowd management during peak festival days.

### घटना का विवरण
शनिवार, 17 अक्टूबर 2026 (महा सप्तमी) की शाम उत्तर कोलकाता स्थित चोरबगान सार्वजनीन दुर्गा पूजा पंडाल में एक दुखद भगदड़ घटी। इस हादसे में कम से कम 19 लोगों की जान चली गई और 25 लोग घायल हो गए। भारी भीड़, अचानक आई बारिश और आयोजकों की ओर से की गई एक घोषणा के बाद बाहर खड़े लोग अचानक आगे बढ़े, जिससे यह हादसा हुआ।

### न्यायिक जांच और प्रशासनिक कार्रवाई
पश्चिम बंगाल के मुख्यमंत्री सुवेंदु अधिकारी ने घोषणा की कि कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय के वर्तमान न्यायाधीश की अध्यक्षता में एक विशेष जांच दल (SIT) इस हादसे की जांच करेगा। राज्य सरकार कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश से इसके लिए न्यायाधीश नामित करने का अनुरोध करेगी। SIT में स्पेशल टास्क फोर्स (STF), आपराधिक जांच विभाग (CID) और अन्य विभागों के अधिकारी शामिल होंगे।

कोलकाता पुलिस के एंटी-राउडी सेक्शन ने घटनाक्रम को समझने के लिए सीसीटीवी फुटेज जब्त कर ली है। भीड़ प्रबंधन में चूक के संबंध में पूछताछ के लिए पूजा समिति के सदस्यों, निजी सुरक्षा गार्डों और ड्यूटी पर तैनात कर्मियों को हिरासत में लिया गया है।

### मुआवजा और राहत उपाय
- **राज्य सरकार की सहायता:** पश्चिम बंगाल सरकार ने मृतक के परिजनों को ₹25 लाख का मुआवजा और एक ग्रुप डी सरकारी नौकरी देने की घोषणा की। घायलों को ₹5 लाख की सहायता और उनकी पसंद के अस्पताल में मुफ्त इलाज की सुविधा मिलेगी।
- **केंद्रीय राहत सहायता:** प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने प्रधानमंत्री राष्ट्रीय राहत कोष (PMNRF) से प्रत्येक मृतक के परिजन को ₹2 लाख और घायलों को ₹50,000 की अनुग्रह राशि देने की घोषणा की।
- **आपातकालीन हेल्पलाइन:** राज्य सरकार ने एक टोल-फ्री हेल्पलाइन (1800-345-5678) और कोलकाता पुलिस ने एक कंट्रोल रूम हेल्पलाइन (033-2214-1310) जारी की है।

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee expressed shock on Saturday over a tragic Kolkata stampede in which at least 17 people lost their lives. The Trinamool Congress (TMC) alleged poor crowd management and a lack of police presence after the stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity puja pandal. The TMC, in a post on X, following the tragic incident, wrote, "No police, no civic volunteers, no ambulances, no crowd management! This is what local residents are stating in the wake of the tragic stampede at Chorebagan Puja Pandal." Follow live updates on the Kolkata stampede here . Deep Dive Targeting the ruling BJP and the police, the party said, "@KolkataPolice and the @BJP4Bengal administration must answer for these grave lapses. Public safety cannot be treated so casually. As the death toll rises, who will take responsibility? Will @SuvenduWB accept accountability and resign?" "On the very day @AmitShah arrives, Bengal is confronted with this heartbreaking tragedy. Shameful state of affairs," it added. Also Read | 17 dead after stampede at Kolkata Durga Puja pandal; CM Suvendu Adhikari reaches hospital 'Little to no police presence to control the crowd': TMC In another X post, the TMC stated that eyewitnesses and local residents reported little to no police presence for crowd control at the Chorebagan Puja Pandal. It said, "@KolkataPolice, WHERE WAS THE SECURITY AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE WHEN PEOPLE NEEDED YOU MOST?" "Eyewitnesses and local residents allege that there was little to no police presence to control the crowd at Chorebagan Puja Pandal. In the aftermath of the stampede, it was ordinary citizens who stepped in to rescue the injured, the party added. It further said, "How many more lives must be put at risk before the @BJP4Bengal administration answers for these failures? Why does public safety take a back seat while VIP arrangements receive priority?" Mamata Banerjee expresses shock Former West Bengal CM Banerjee posted on X wishing a speedy recovery of the injured individuals in the stampede. The TMC chief said, "Deeply shocked and saddened to learn about the stampede at the Chore Bagan Puja Pandal." "I pray to Maa Durga for the speedy recovery of all those injured and for strength and courage for their families during this difficult time," she added. "Today at around 7:40 pm, a stampede occurred at the exit gate of Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Puja Pandal, under Girish Park Police Station, due to heavy crowds of pandal hoppers amid rainfall. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences over the deaths in Kolkata stampede while wishing recovery to those injured in the incident. The prime minister assured of all possible aid to the victims.

“The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest. The local administration is providing all possible assistance to those affected,” the PMO said in a tweet on Saturday.

At least 17 people died in a stampede Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity puja pandal in Kolkata. The pandal was subsequently closed and so were some others that were registering a massive footfall.

Apart from PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah, Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also expressed condolences.

news.headline: Indore BJP official booked under POCSO for misbehaving with girl at Garba venue
news.story_lead: Indore BJP official booked under POCSO for misbehaving with girl at Garba venue Accused Kamal Chauhan is a supporter of MLA Ramesh Mendola and was assigned duty to manage arrangements at the Garba venue at Kankeshwari Ground in Indore. BJP mandal president Kamal Chauhan, who allegedly pushed and misbehaved with a 15-year-old girl at a Garba venue, was booked under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and molestation charges in Indore on Saturday. Chauhan is a supporter of MLA Ramesh Mendola.

The party has also taken cognizance after the video of the incident went viral and served a show cause notice. The party state president Hemant Khandelwal asked him to reply within three days. Heeranagar town inspector KK Sharma said the minor girl from Khatipura had filed complaint against Kamal Chauhan. “On Thursday night, the girl had gone to watch Garba. The entire incident happened in front of the girl's family members,” said the TI. A video of it went viral on social media. Taking cognizance, police on Saturday recorded the girl's statement and registered an FIR against Chauhan. However, Chauhan said his intention was not to misbehave with the girl. “It happened while managing the pandal after argument heated up with the family for taking entry with pass.”

news.full_article_text: Government doctor among 3 arrested as Rajasthan ANTF seizes 3.764 kg of raw MD Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force arrested a government doctor and two others after busting an alleged mephedrone manufacturing unit in Balotra. A government doctor was among three people arrested after Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) busted an alleged mephedrone (MD) manufacturing unit at a house in Balotra district on Saturday. Police seized 3.764 kg of raw MD, chemicals and equipment, ₹ 3.41 lakh in cash and a car. The ANTF team, with assistance from local police, raided the premises in the Siwana police station area after receiving information about an alleged MD manufacturing unit, deputy inspector general of police Abhijeet Singh said. Police identified the three arrested men as prime suspect Suresh Kumar Vishnoi (27), a resident of Mithora; Dr Mukesh Vishnoi (29), and Utkarsh Vishnoi (19), a resident of Modran village in Jalore district. From failed government job aspirant to alleged MD manufacturer Suresh completed his graduation and attempted several government recruitment examinations, including those for patwari, gram sevak, Rajasthan Police, forest guard and police sub-inspector posts, but failed to secure a government job, an ANTF officer said. In 2022, he moved to Bengaluru with a friend and began working in pharmaceutical sales as a medical representative. After working in the field for around two years, he allegedly found the earnings insufficient. Police said Suresh returned to his village in 2024 and came into contact with people involved in drug trafficking. He allegedly began purchasing, selling and supplying MD before deciding to manufacture it himself in pursuit of higher profits. Investigators suspect that he learnt the process of manufacturing MD by watching videos on YouTube and other social media platforms. He allegedly used chemicals and equipment to prepare the drug at his house in Mithora. According to the ANTF, Suresh had called Dr Mukesh Vishnoi and Utkarsh Vishnoi to his house to sell a consignment of MD. The two allegedly arrived in a car. news.full_article_text: - Published 17 October 2026, 03:33 BST Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue. Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro. Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon. Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%. The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil. Why the Amazon rainforest is so important What in the World podcast Jair Bolsonaro promoted mining in indigenous lands in the Amazon and forest clearances soared at the same time as resources to protect the forest were cut. During Bolsonaro's presidency from 2019 to 2022, the Amazon lost nearly 60% more in forest lands compared to the previous four years, news agency AFP reported, citing official data. Lula reversed his policies and oversaw deforestation rates drop to a six-year low during his first year in office. Lula tightened up environmental monitoring and penalties for illegal logging. "Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," he said in a post on X on Friday. Tropical rainforests like the Amazon are home to millions of species. In a healthy state, they absorb vast quantities of planet-warming carbon dioxide, helping to keep the Earth cool. But they have come under increasing pressure from decades of deliberate land clearance for agriculture and logging, as well as climate change, which scientists warn can create conditions for wildfires. Brazil's Environment Minister Joao Paulo Capobianco described the decline in Amazon deforestation as "absolutely stratospheric". It was an "historic achievement" for Brazil, said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima. It showed that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions", Astrini said. news.headline: Supreme Court Directs Centre to Launch Portal for Autism Stem Cell Therapy Patients
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India has ordered the Union Government to establish a dedicated online portal within six weeks for patients undergoing stem cell therapy for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The order mandates the creation of a comprehensive database to track patients, clinics, and medical practitioners while enforcing strict regulatory oversight on unauthorized clinical services.
news.full_article_text:
### Regulatory Mandate for Stem Cell Therapy in ASD

A Supreme Court bench comprising Justices JB Pardiwala and R Mahadevan issued key directions to the Union Government regarding stem cell therapy for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Building upon its January 30, 2026 ruling—which banned stem cell therapy as a routine clinical service and restricted it strictly to approved research and clinical trials—the court directed the government to set up a central online portal within six weeks.

### Portal Registration and Temporary Arrangements

- **Target Beneficiaries**: Patients who began stem cell therapy for ASD on or before January 30, 2026, are required to register on the portal.
- **Data Requirements**: Practitioners, clinics, parents, and caregivers must maintain detailed medical records, practitioner details, intervention courses, and clinical progress on the portal with strict confidentiality safeguards.
- **Temporary Continuity**: Registered patients whose therapy started on or prior to January 30, 2026, will be permitted to continue therapy as a strictly temporary arrangement until a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) is established. The court emphasized that this does not constitute official approval or recognition of stem cell therapy as an established clinical service.

### Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) Framework

In response to earlier directions, the Centre submitted an affidavit on September 28 disclosing that no applications for clinical trials had been received since January 30. The Centre proposed a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR):

- **Sites**: Two tertiary care facilities—one in North India and one in South India.
- **Timeline**: To be established within six months.
- **Court Observations**: The court noted that the proposed RCT lacked clear eligibility criteria for existing patients and directed the Centre to formulate a monitoring plan for excluded patients. Additionally, the Parents’ Forum for Stem Cells in Autism and Cerebral Palsy was permitted to submit suggestions on the trial design.

### Public Information and Legal Awareness

The court criticized the lack of readily available public information regarding regulatory restrictions, which allowed unauthorized clinics and practitioners to offer stem cell treatments. To address this, the Centre was given six weeks to publish a comprehensive protocol on stem cell use in ASD research and clinical trials. Furthermore, a dedicated section must be added to the Ministry of Health's official website explaining the legal status and regulatory requirements in clear, accessible language. The Union Government must submit a compliance report prior to the next hearing scheduled for December 14.

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने केंद्र सरकार को ऑटिज्म स्पेक्ट्रम डिसऑर्डर (ASD) के लिए स्टेम सेल थेरेपी करा रहे मरीजों के लिए छह सप्ताह के भीतर एक समर्पित ऑनलाइन पोर्टल शुरू करने का निर्देश दिया है। अदालत ने मरीजों, क्लीनिकों और डॉक्टरों का एक विस्तृत डेटाबेस बनाए रखने का आदेश दिया है ताकि अनधिकृत इलाज पर रोक लगाई जा सके।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### ऑटिज्म स्टेम सेल थेरेपी के लिए नियामक निर्देश

जस्टिस जेबी पारदीवाला और जस्टिस आर महादेवन की पीठ ने ऑटिज्म स्पेक्ट्रम डिसऑर्डर (ASD) के लिए स्टेम सेल थेरेपी के इस्तेमाल पर केंद्र सरकार को सख्त निर्देश दिए हैं। अपने 30 जनवरी 2026 के आदेश को आगे बढ़ाते हुए, जिसमें सामान्य नैदानिक सेवा के रूप में स्टेम सेल थेरेपी पर रोक लगाई गई थी, अदालत ने छह सप्ताह के भीतर एक समर्पित पोर्टल स्थापित करने का आदेश दिया।

### पोर्टल पंजीकरण और अस्थायी व्यवस्था

- **पात्र मरीज**: 30 जनवरी 2026 को या उससे पहले स्टेम सेल थेरेपी शुरू करने वाले मरीजों का पंजीकरण पोर्टल पर अनिवार्य है।
- **आवश्यक विवरण**: डॉक्टरों, क्लीनिकों, और अभिभावकों को मरीज का मेडिकल रिकॉर्ड और उपचार का विवरण पोर्टल पर दर्ज करना होगा।
- **अस्थायी छूट**: पंजीकृत मरीज केवल एक सख्त अस्थायी व्यवस्था के रूप में तब तक इलाज जारी रख सकते हैं जब तक कि रैंडमाइज्ड कंट्रोल ट्रायल (RCT) स्थापित नहीं हो जाता।

### क्लिनिकल ट्रायल और शोध रूपरेखा

केंद्र सरकार ने 28 सितंबर को दिए हलफनामे में बताया कि 30 जनवरी के बाद क्लिनिकल ट्रायल का कोई आवेदन प्राप्त नहीं हुआ है। केंद्र ने ICMR द्वारा वित्तपोषित एक बहु-केंद्रीकृत ट्रायल का प्रस्ताव रखा है जो उत्तर और दक्षिण भारत के दो अस्पतालों में छह महीने के भीतर शुरू होगा।

### सार्वजनिक जागरूकता और दिशानिर्देश

अदालत ने कहा कि सही जानकारी के अभाव में अवैध क्लीनिक फल-फूल रहे हैं। इसलिए केंद्र को छह सप्ताह के भीतर नियम पुस्तिका जारी करने और स्वास्थ्य मंत्रालय की वेबसाइट पर स्पष्ट सार्वजनिक सूचना डालने का निर्देश दिया गया है। मामले की अगली सुनवाई 14 दिसंबर को होगी।
